findings.title: Hardcoded AWS access key committed to source
findings.evidence: A module-level constant is assigned a literal AWS access key ID in the deploy script: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "[REDACTED-AWS-KEY]"'.
findings.recommendation: Remove the literal and load credentials from the environment or an IAM role: let boto3 use its default provider chain (env vars, ~/.aws/credentials, instance/task role). If a key was ever real, rotate/revoke it and purge it from history (the value must be treated as compromised the moment it lands in a commit). Add a secret-scanning pre-commit hook / CI check so this cannot recur.

findings.title: Constant has no effect on the boto3 client it appears to configure
findings.evidence: The key is assigned to a module constant, but the client is then created without any explicit credential argument: 'client = boto3.client("s3", region_name=REGION)'. boto3 resolves credentials from its provider chain (env vars, shared config, IAM role), not from module attributes, so the constant is dead code that only leaks the secret without making the deploy use it.
findings.recommendation: Drop the constant entirely and rely on the default credential chain; if explicit credentials are genuinely required, pass them via os.environ lookups or boto3.Session(profile_name=...), and fail fast with a clear error when the credential source is missing.
